dossier.public_summary: The dip is exactly the same length of time as the star spins (~1.64 days) and its depth jumps by a factor of >2 between sectors, even flipping negative, while the star varies by tens of thousands of ppm. This shows the signal tracks the star's spots, not a planet transiting. The duration and grazing shape also mismatch a planet on this small star.

reasons.why: Depth changes catastrophically within each pipeline: 3640/3753 ppm in sectors 15/16 vs 9243/7555 ppm in sectors 22/23 (depth_change_pct 243.7, sectors.p_constant 0) and also steady depth ~5000 ppm in sectors 75/76 vs negative depths in sectors 48/49. A planet transit depth cannot flip by this amount between sectors, including sign reversal.
reasons.value: verdict: changes_within_a_source, p_constant_all: 0.0, by_source SPOC 2-min p_constant: 9.351171918175925e-265, TESS-SPOC p_constant: 0.0

reasons.why: Signal period is 1.63759 d, statistically identical to the star's spot period 1.642 d in all 8 sectors, with huge spotted modulation (~4-8% vs dip ~5102 ppm) and phase_curve amplitude_ppm 1822 ratio_to_depth 0.3571 chi2 1713 dof 9, indicating the dip is part of the stellar variability, not a transit.

Transit shape is grazing (impact 0.9177, v_sigma -19.28) and duration 2.487 h is much longer than central_h 1.733 h (ratio 1.435) with large chi2_red 8.371 and density penalty, inconsistent with a planetary transit on a 0.7029 Rsun K dwarf.

Centroid is formally on_target, but shape and variability favor a stellar-origin doppelgaenger rather than a blended binary. Low planet_rank and 4/5 similar labelled candidates 'not a planet' support the variability-as-transit interpretation; centroid alone does not overcome the variable-depth and period-equality evidence.
